mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than -0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime that erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in housing starts (HOUST) above a 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months where HOUST is above its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumer spending but also increases wage pressures, resulting in a positive S&P 500 return over the next 5 trading days only if wage inflation remains muted (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY).
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND UNRATE < 5% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY
regime_hint: expansion with slack and low wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS and UNRATE rise while CPIAUCSL remains below 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a deepening consumer demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months where RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average.
